Both traces correctly identify the graph as uncolorable with 3 channels by finding a K4 subgraph. Trace 1 derives the contradiction by focusing on F's neighbors and the triangle {C, D, I}, concluding {C, D, I, F} is a K4. It then loops to re-derive this exact logical contradiction. Trace 2 finds the K4 {C, D, F, I} directly and then finds another K4 {A, F, G, I}. Trace 2 diverges by extensively re-verifying the prompt's edges and even exploring hypothetical missing edges to see if the graph could be colorable. This divergence (a CYCLE) pays off only in reinforcing Trace 2's confidence in the K4 structure, whereas Trace 1's divergence is a LOOP that re-derives the same conclusion without exploring new alternatives. Neither divergence changes the final answer, but Trace 2's approach is more empirical while Trace 1's is more logical.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let me double check the edges to be absolutely sure." end="Therefore, no valid assignment exists." basis="The solver re-executes the proof that {C, D, I} forms a triangle and F connects to all, leading to the same contradiction it already derived just prior to this span."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's try to verify if I missed an edge or misread a letter in the input string provided in the prompt." end="Given 3 channels, it's impossible." basis="The solver re-checks the edges of the clique {C, D, F, I} which it already verified in the preceding paragraph."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Wait, let me check the clique {C, D, F, I} again." end="So yes, K4." basis="Re-verification of the same clique edges for the third time."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let's try to find a solution on the assumption that I made a mistake and the graph IS 3-colorable." end="So the clique {A,F,G,I} is robust." basis="The solver explores the alternative that the graph is 3-colorable if an edge is missing, checks which edge would make it colorable, and eliminates the branch by confirming the edge is present, reinforcing the K4 structure."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let me double check the clique {A, F, G, I} one more time." end="Yes, all edges are explicitly listed." basis="Re-verification of the edges of the {A, F, G, I} clique, adding no new information."
